name: Semi truck
headline: length
subtitle: Tractor with a long-haul semitrailer (interstate design vehicle)
description: A semi truck is a tractor unit pulling a semitrailer. Road designers use the WB-67 'interstate' design vehicle, with a 67 ft wheelbase and an overall length of about 74 ft, to represent long-haul tractor-trailers. Federal rules set the width at 102 inches on the National Network and the gross weight limit at 80,000 lb, while height limits are set by the states.

measures.label: Overall length (WB-67 design vehicle)
measures.note: Long-haul tractor-semitrailer that road designers plan for; real rigs vary

measures.label: Height (typical state limits)
measures.note: Most state height limits range from 13 ft 6 in to 14 ft; there is no federal height limit

measures.label: Width (federal limit)
measures.note: Width that states must allow on the National Network

measures.label: Minimum semitrailer length states must allow
measures.note: Federal minimum for the semitrailer in a tractor-semitrailer combination

facts.text: States may not impose an overall length limit on a tractor-semitrailer combination on the National Network.

sources.title: Federal Size Regulations for Commercial Motor Vehicles (FHWA-HOP-04-022)
Vehicle Size and Weight Program Overview

caveats: Tractor-trailer lengths vary with the tractor and trailer. The 74 ft figure is the WB-67 design vehicle that road designers use for long-haul trucks.
